hook: The best thing a dermatologist ever told me was to stop buying so much.

beats.vo: The best thing a dermatologist ever told me was to stop buying so much.
beats.visual: Car interior, daylight, she turns the appointment card over in her fingers.

avatar_brief: Woman 46-54, at a kitchen table with a laptop open on a skincare brand's ingredients page. Reading glasses on. Delivery is precise and a little pedantic in a likeable way — she is the friend who actually looks things up.
hook: I finally looked up what 'dermatologist tested' legally means. It's less than you'd hope and more than nothing.
first_frame: Over her shoulder at a laptop showing a product ingredients page, her finger on the trackpad, glasses on.

beats.vo: I finally looked up what 'dermatologist tested' legally means. It's less than you'd hope and more than nothing.
beats.visual: Laptop screen, she scrolls an ingredients page.

beats.vo: It means a dermatologist oversaw testing for irritation. It doesn't mean one endorsed it. Those are different sentences.
beats.visual: She turns to camera, glasses coming off.

beats.vo: Which matters, because on mature skin the thing that goes wrong first is usually irritation, not ageing.
beats.visual: Cut to the night balm jar on the table beside the laptop.

beats.vo: This one's dermatologist-tested, it's rosehip and marigold in beeswax, and it softens the look of fine lines.
beats.visual: She opens it, works a little between her fingers — dense, slow.

beats.vo: Thirty-seven dollars. I'd rather have the honest claim than the impressive one.
beats.visual: Laptop closed, jar in the centre of the table.

beats.vo: Wrinkle Smoothing Night Balm, from Frøya. Go and read what yours actually says.
beats.visual: Jar held to camera, brand name on screen.

cta: Wrinkle Smoothing Night Balm, from Frøya. Go and read what yours actually says.
